text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today as oil prices weakened on news that the G7 will release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over the next four months to ease fuel supply constraints. This supply injection directly pressures crude prices—US oil dropped to $96.16 per barrel—which cuts into profits for oil producers like ConocoPhillips. The stock has drifted down 3.85% over the past two weeks, tracking this gradual softening in the energy market.

Offsetting some of that pressure is geopolitical tension that typically supports oil prices: the U.S. is deploying additional military assets to the Middle East and considering renewed strikes on Iran, which usually tightens supply concerns. However, today the supply-relief story from the G7 outweighed those bullish signals, leaving the stock slightly underwater.
